question: Does USE_ISO_MALLOC=OFF (the drop's PlayStation port default) put the 834 WTF_MAKE_ISO_ALLOCATED classes in the general heap, and does the oracle's build have IsoHeap?

verdicts.reason: USE_ISO_MALLOC 0 from the port default; the ISO macro is WTF_MAKE_FAST_ALLOCATED and the 834 classes are in the general bmalloc heap
verdicts.confidence: source-level, single-site; a Sony build script could still pass -DUSE_ISO_MALLOC=ON and the drop contains no other reference, so the shipped binary's value is not readable from the drop

verdicts.reason: cmakeconfig.h:211 USE_SYSTEM_MALLOC 1 takes the first arm even though the cache says USE_ISO_MALLOC ON; fastMalloc is void* fastMalloc(size_t){... malloc(n) ...} (FastMalloc.cpp:156,236; fastFree -> free at :265)
verdicts.confidence: measured at object level and library level

verdicts.reason: stripped (0 .symtab sections); hidden-visibility class allocators are absent from .dynsym by construction, so neither symbol table can answer

oracle_object.iso_on_control: not built - with USE_SYSTEM_MALLOC 0 the TU needs bmalloc/GigacageConfig.h, which this build dir has never generated

scope_corrections: Source/WebCore/css/CSSFontFace.h:61 is WTF_MAKE_FAST_ALLOCATED_WITH_HEAP_IDENTIFIER, not WTF_MAKE_ISO_ALLOCATED: docs/65's object was never an ISO class, so none of its verdicts depended on this gate.
Source/WebCore/html/canvas/CanvasRenderingContext2D.h:37 and CanvasRenderingContext2DBase.h:93 are WTF_MAKE_ISO_ALLOCATED, so the class in the console case c043b is governed by the gate.
Source/JavaScriptCore contains no reference to USE(ISO_MALLOC); JSC's IsoSubspace (docs/76's stringSpace) is its own cell space and docs/76 stands either way.

c043b (alias at spray index 2 of 80) cannot discriminate IsoHeap from a type-agnostic bmalloc size-class free list: both reuse a freed slot for the same class. The discriminating input is a cross-type allocation of the same size class, which only the console can run.
